dialog.text: I spoke with my agent about getting you in on my next photo shoot.
Oh my gosh, did you really? Wow! I really appreciate that. What did they say?
They said they're having trouble finding reliable models with a more mature look, and would be happy to give you a shot at the shoot.
So they don't think I'm too old? That is amazing news. This is a dream come true for me! I'm so excited! I cannot thank you enough.

Not at all - the industry is a little saturated with shallow 20-somethings that all look the same, so there is a certain niche that they're trying to fill in order to appeal to the older crowd. And it's no problem - I'm just the middleman! Ultimately the credit is yours. I'm sure you'll do great.

Okay, I see. Well, I guess I'm in luck then. Here I always thought that I was too old to model and now I learn that they actually want people that look older. Amazing. Has your agent found any new jobs for you lately?

A common misconception - many clothing companies, for example, that have older demographics use models within that age group in order to better promote their clothes. A lot of people can do it, just a matter of finding those opportunities that exist. But anyway - my agent has arranged for a photoshoot to help promote the new Tony Hawk game! I'm super pumped.
You should be pumped! That sounds like a really cool opportunity! Do you get to do that soon?
It's in Los Angeles in about two weeks from now. Cast should be off before then. It'll be nice to visit my dad while I'm there, too; I haven't seen him in a while.
How's your dad doing? Gosh, I haven't seen him in forever! I'm sure it'll be really nice to visit him. Will you do any sightseeing?

I was starting to worry about being homeless!

I'd love a break but I'm going to stay on at the bar, picking up as many extra shifts as possible for more money. Have you decided if you're going back to school yet?  If so, I know a great apartment that has your name on it!
I have sent my application in so fingers crossed. Would that be an apartment near the nursing college? Is your friend moving out next year?

She is.  She's graduating early and will be moving out this summer.  So if you're interested, it's yours!  And I'm hardly there so it would be almost like your own place.  Sound promising or should I think about advertising for a roomie soon?

I am interested! This would be amazing and I couldn't ask for a better flatmate. It would be interesting to see the apartment again too. I find out about my application early next month so I can confirm it then. Are you OK to hold on advertising until then?

Absolutely.  Any time you want to see the place, just let me know.  If I'm not around, my roommate might.  Afterwards, I could should you around and point out all the best places to eat.  Do you Thai or pizza?  I found the best restaurants and both offer delivery. It's the absolute best for late night studying!

I don't need to the see apartment but it would great to meet up. I'm next weekend if you have time. Which food do I like the best? I love Thai food, it's so full of flavors although I have to confess I do order quite a few pizzas! New York is amazing for deliveries. Everything is so convenient.

I know right?!  We just discovered a late night cookie delivery business!  They will also bring you milk and ice cream.  I don't know why anyone would not want to live here or in NY.  What about music?  Do you like going to live shows?  If so, the bar where I work, has live performances every Sat night and there's another great place that has live music every night.

Cookie delivery! What more could you ask for. I do like live music. Do you want to catch a performance next week? I'm wondering if you'd prefer to go somewhere other than your work bar! What do you think? Are there any good nights coming up?

dialog.text: How's your dog doing Nancy?

He's doing OK. After a couple of days of resting and generally looking a bit forlorn he's bounced back to his normal self. Most importantly. his wet nose has returned. A dog with a dry nose is not a happy dog.
That's wonderful news. I'm glad he's back to his usual self. How was the bee farm?

Very interesting. I never knew bees were so fascinating. They had hives with glass backs that were illuminated under special lights so we can look in see what was happening. There so much going on inside. Also I learned just how much work it takes to make honey! So many trips by the bee to make just a small amount of honey. I think they have caught my interest!

Nice! That's really cool that they designed the hives like that. I wonder how it looks at night. Thanks for the idea, I may have to configure some of my own hives that way too! But yes, bees are very fascinating and such hard workers, as odd as that may sound.
Do you do bee rescues for people with bees nesting on their properties?

Sometimes! In a rural setting, there's not too many neighbors for it to happen very often. But generally once or twice a year they seem to start nesting in a place they shouldn't be. I don't mind removing them for free. Saves some bees and adds to my colony.

I've watched some videos about this after my farm visit and I've some questions. How do get most of the bees into the transport hives before moving them? What happens to the bees that get left behind, do they die or can they join another hive near by? I feel really sorry for any bees that get left behind. Imagine coming back to find your whole community has moved. As you can see I am starting to fall in love with bees!!

It helps to having a non-lethal freezing compound that kind of keeps them in place when removing and transporting the hives. We try not to leave any behind, but inevitably some do. Those bees tend to attempt a rebuild of the hive, generally in the same vicinity. Bees are oddly territorial so it is unlikely that they stand any chance besides that. But yeah that would be odd, it would be like the apocalypse for bees. And no doubt - bees are amazing critters!

It never occurred to me that they would rebuild a hive. Can they do that without a queen? I've heard of hives that have lost their queens but never quite understood what the consequences of that would be. Does it mean the hive can't produce any new bees?

They can, yes. It's sort of a little makeshift mini-hive, not really a full-blown hive. It helps when people follow-up that way we can come back later on to collect the stragglers. And it means exactly that - the Queen is responsible for laying larva, but an already-established colony of bees can technically sustain itself for a period of time, of course just until they reach the end of their lifespans.

I see, so if a hive is rebuilt in the same location then you can be confident they were from the original hive and collect them to be rejoin their friends. That never occurred to me. The bees certainly seem to be very resilient. How did you first get in to caring for bees?

I would love some. Natural honey isn't pasteurized is it?

No, it's right from my hive. It's really excellent, too. Some of the best I've gotten from them. But I just can't eat it all by myself and you know my wife won't have any! Can't risk the model figure.
I've heard natural honey is really good at protecting people from allergies. Have you heard this too?
Oh definitely! Locally sourced honey is one of the best natural allergy fighters out there. The fact that it's super tasty doesn't hurt either.
Maybe you can convince your wife to eat some for the allergy benefits!!!
Yeah, she's pretty lucky in that area -- no real allergies. Must be her Italian blood. The honey definitely helps with my hay fever.

Sure, I could do that! I'm supposed to go tomorrow morning to rescue a hive that set up shop in this lady's yard. She's not too happy about it but I'm thrilled to get more bees!
How hard is it to rescue a hive?

As long as you know what you're doing, it's not too hard, but it can definitely be time consuming. It kind of depends on the circumstances. The last one I rescued had gotten into the walls of the house so there was a lot of work that had to be done there.

Haha if only we could get Cesar to help us out! I'm sure both our dogs would be trained in no time.

Very courageous for training aggressive dogs, too!!

dialog.text: How is your new job as a life coach going? Should be your 2nd week right?
Thank you for asking, I love it! It has been very rewarding to connect and help people!
What is your most favorite aspect of the job so far? It must be really fulfilling. I would love to be able to feel that kind of fulfillment in my daily work,

I think the most rewarding part is the personal connection I feel with my clients. When another person opens up to you, it is as healing to me as to them! I am sure you will be very fulfilled once you become a physical therapist.
Yes, I hope so. Do you have any other advice for someone just starting out? I want to soak up as much knowledge from you as I can!

I was taught to be as open and humble as I can approaching each new client. This allows them to feel comfortable and understood! And for you becoming a physical therapist, I was suggest letting them open up about their pain and hardships as much as they want.
Yes, I think I need to learn how to be more approachable to people. I find it hard right now. I am not much of a people person, which makes me question my career choice!
I am sure your schooling will help you learn to approach and connect to your clients. There are classes and weekend shops that help with that. Don't give up on your career choice!
I sure hope so! It is very stressful. I think I need to take some time to relax and unwind this weekend. Any ideas?
I could imagine it is stressful! How about running. I know you are preparing for a 5k. Maybe a good run will help clear your mind.
Yes, that is a good idea. It will help me train and also pump those endorphins. I am trying to figure out what other exercise to incorporate into my training.
I think running is my best form of therapy! I do a lengthy amount of stretching before and after. I also use resistance bands in my workouts

Work is going well - people have been very generous lately with the tips!  How about for you - any new book recommendations from the book store?

Oh, I enjoy a good murder mystery as well!  I have ridden my motorcycle lately.  I won't be riding for a while, though...I fell off and broke my leg!

I'm in Texas.  Lot's of rain right now, but I know the heat is coming soon.  The weather has been so crazy this year.  Jeremy and Leon, those are great names.  My dog is named Georgie and my cat is Kitty-cat.  I know, not very original for a cat.  Georgie is named after George Washington because he is very presidential.  Are Jeremy and Leon named after anyone in particular?
I thought Jeremy was funny because he's a German Shepherd. And Leon the Lab, my kids picked that name. Does Georgie like the rain?

No, poor Georgie is a Yorkie - he's so small that anytime it rains he feels like he's going to drown in all the puddles.  It's funny because he does like going to the beach with me. You ever take your dogs to the beach?
Aw poor guy! Yes, I live in New England so the beach is never more than an hour away. They go to the beach often during the summer. They love the waves. Is yours afraid of the waves?

I don't think he is afraid of them - he loves to run up and bark at them, and then run away as they come ashore. He's really funny to watch, like he thinks he can make the waves not come in.  Though I don't think our gulf waves are as exciting as anything in New England though.  I do love being at the beach, no matter where.
Does he bark a lot? Mine bark at pretty much everything that moves.
Oh yeah.  He barks constantly.  I don't even hear it anymore, but when my sister comes over it drives her crazy! If fact she's coming over tonight to test out a new pasta recipe I'm making.
Oh delicious! What's in it?
Well pasta made from scratch of course, and then a basil pesto with mushrooms and cherry tomatoes, topped with freshly grated cheese. Do you think I should add some type of seafood to it too?

Kimchi is great! And really beneficial for the digestive and immune systems, I understand. Has something to do with intestinal flora and fauna. When you get it down, let me know how to do it.

Heh, that sounds both reasonable and modern! Leave some space in the Mason jar for the fermentation gases.
Good point! What's your first meal on the outside?

dialog.text: I am almost done shopping for the triplets

I'm sure you're going to just fine!! It sounds like you're getting very prepared for when they come. It sounds like you weren't planning three at the least. Were you trying to conceive or did it just happen?

Well kids were always part of the plan and we were trying for a few months, but we never imagine we would have triplets! I was hoping to have a boy and a girl like a typical family but now we're going to have an extra member!

There's no controlling when or what gender you'll conceive. I'm sure you'll love them all the same. Three does sound like a handful, though. I hope your husband is the helping type! It does take a village to raise a child as they say! Have you had baby shower for them, yet?

Yes my husband helps so much with the shopping and getting the house ready for the babies, he does everything I can't do and more! We were actually planning a baby shower for August 20th, maybe I'd see you there?

That sounds great! I would love to come! Where will you be having it at? Since you've done so much shopping is there anything you need that you haven't purchased, yet? If not, I'll bring a couple watches. One for the lady and one for the husband. Maybe, both.
We're just going to have it at our place, maybe show off the new baby room! We have a registry if you want to check it out but some watches from your company would be a personal touch.
That sounds great. I'll have to check out your registry. Is the baby room a specific theme? I'm sure three cribs is taking up a lot of space. That must be a big room!

We didn't try to go with a theme since the three of them will be living with each other for while and interests might clash haha. It's a decently big room but luckily there were some small triplet cribs that connect together to fit on one wall. We also have a triple bunk for when they're older!

I hadn't thought about maroon, that's an interesting idea. I had been thinking about greens and yellows to just be neutral. What do you think about those colors? Maybe with some patterns?
Oh, those would work really well! I think a lovely yellow would give it all a sunshiney feeling. How would you feel about sorta star-shaped or sun-shaped patterns and such?

dialog.text: How are you and the cats?
Things are not great. My one cat, Hugo is getting really old and we think he is sick. I have to take him to the vet this week.
I'm so sorry to hear that! How old is he?
He is 15 years old, and is the oldest of my three. It is so sad when they get to this age! How old are your cats?

That's so hard! You love giving them a long life but it sure is hard to watch them age. My oldest cat is my tabby, Ginger. She's 11. My tortiseshell Baxter is only 7 but he acts like a grumpy old man already.
Aw, I love how they have different personalities. Have you had both of them since they were kittens? How do they interact with your kids?

Yes, both as kittens! I got Ginger before my sons were born, but my oldest was one when we got Baxter. They get along well, for the most part since they basically grew up together. Did you get yours as kittens?

Yes, Hugo has been with me since he was only a few weeks old, so he is very special to me. He's my Russian Blue. My Japanese Bobtail is named Potato, and I got her as a kitten as well. The only one I didn't get as a kitten is Frank, my Birman cat, and that's because I adopted him from a friend who found him as a stray. It's adorable that your cats grew up with your kids!

I love the name Potato! I bet she's adorable. I would love to adopt a stray. I think the next cat I take in will be a rescue of some sort. I'm really sorry Hugo isn't doing well. I hope the vet is able to give you some answers at his appointment.
Thank you for the well wishes. I am hoping he is ok too, and am very anxious to hear what the vet says. Are you thinking of getting another cat any time soon?

Well I will be thinking of you two! I'm considering it. We're trying to get pregnant with one more child, but I think if that doesn't happen in the next few months we might take in another cat. Especially as Ginger gets older, I want Baxter to have another companion. Do your cats get along well?

That's a great song! And yeah, my kids and my cats keep me company. We've got a full, lively house!
Are you thinking on adding on, now that you have another one on the way?
Probably not. I think we're done. We've got plenty of humans and animals in our home. By the way, tell me more about your cats. What are their names?

Ah, gotcha. Hmm, we haven't really considered that, though I'd be open to the idea. Any pointers? Also, those are wonderful names!
Well, adding a room onto your house could be a big project depending on the style of your house. I'd be happy to advise if you want. Have you thought about baby names yet?
Maybe we can set up a call to talk about expanding our house! You could even be our contractor! And not yet--I'll need to ask my husband. Maybe my sons also have some good ideas!
I bet your boys could have some really creative baby names to suggest. If you decide you want to move forward, either I can help or I can refer you to someone in your area.

dialog.text: Man, I just sold a bunch of my vegetables on Facebook.
Outstanding. I have never used Facebook Marketplace. Was it easy?
Surprisingly so. I know it can seem intimidating at first! IT was definitely a different experience than running a roadside stand! You should try to sell some of your products online!

I would be worried about the transfer of goods for money. No matter who sends their part first, what if the other party doesn't? It would feel like you were robbed. And YOUR vegetables could end up rotting while you waited for a resolution. Was that a concern for you?
You bring up so great points! I was able to schedule a safe pick up with the customers. I sent one of my farm workers there and he said it went smooth as butter!
So do you like Facebook Marketplace BETTER than your roadside stand?
Ehhh not necessarily. It does broaden my demographic though. I am able to reach many more customers through Facebook. Some of them have never even seen my roadside stand. Can you believe it?!

Sure. Facebook is worldwide, and the roadside stand depends on who drives by. But if your Facebook transactions also require face-to-face meetings to transfer goods, I guess those customers are still relatively local?
Some of them! My employee said that a few people drove from almost 45 minutes away! Sometimes you forget how far you are out in the country.

LOL. I bet!! I'm going to ask the teachers at the culinary school I attend what they think about buying from Facebook Marketplace versus a roadside stand or even a supermarket. It might be interesting to hear their opinions!
That's a great idea! I am very curious to hear what they have to say about it. Where do they sell most of their products?

You know, I don't know if the SCHOOL sells what we make there or not. I usually either just eat my own stuff (probably more than I should) or take it home to give away to my friends. I feel like I need to get better before trying to sell my "attempts".

dialog.text: How did your job interviews go?

That would be great. I'm sure your daughter would love it! It sounds like you already know which hospital you want to get a job at. Maybe while you're at the barbecue; I can help your daughter with her studies in math?

That would be amazing of you. You'd really be giving me a day off. I could use it after those interviews! What can I bring to go with the meat you grill? I have a few nice wines that would go well with meat, or I make a mean batch of brownies.
Brownies sound lovely! I don't really need much, so desserts sound great. I have a freezer full of meats, so no worries there! What kind of desserts do you think you could bring?
I can bring some ice cream to go with the brownies. I also heard you can grill pound cake. Want me to bring some to try that on your grill too?
That would be great! Brownies with ice cream on is one of my favorites. Since your daughter struggles with math, is she failing or does she have a tutor?
She isn't failing, but I haven't hired a tutor. I usually work through problems with her on weekends, because I'm so busy during the week with work. Do you think a tutor would be a good idea?

I think a tutor would be great. It would probably be better than me trying to help. I'm not very good at teaching people stuff, but doesn't mean it's not worth the try. They would be more likely to get her to understand the methods on how to get to the answer. Probably, show her easier ways to do it, too.

Sometimes I feel bad that I can't help her more. You would think a surgeon would be better with math, but it's harder to explain the concepts than to do it in my head. You would probably be better at it than I am. Are you good at Algebra? That's what she's started lately.

Algebra is pretty simple to understand if it's taught to you correctly. It gets confusing when they start mixing the letters with the numbers. I'm sure you do just fine with trying to teach her. Is it harder to teach her the concepts since it's just a message relayed fast in your brain? It does take a lot of math to be a surgeon, doesn't it?

It took a lot of math classes to my Bachelor's Degree in Chemistry before I went to medical school. It sounds silly, but Algebra has become so automatic for my mind that it's hard to break it down into simpler steps. Maybe if I had more time, I'd be better at it. Did you take many math classes?

dialog.text: I have to get the brakes on my new car repaired after the accident. Any news about the bookstore?
Some new books just arrived that I'm eager to check into. What happened with the accident?

I got rear-ended leaving a parking lot the other day. It wasn't a bad accident and there was no obvious damage, but unfortunately my brakes have been a little out of whack ever since. I'm so annoyed but it could have been much worse. I just figured I would let you know, but we don't need to get too much into it! Do you usually end up buying a lot of books from the store you work at? What kinds of new ones are you excited about?
I am glad you are ok. Get those brakes fixed ASAP. I don't get to buy books for the bookstore but I get to read and review them. I love a good thriller book. How's your job at the restaurant going?

That's actually a pretty good perk! Do you read them so you can share your recommendations with customers? The restaurant has been somewhat slow this week, but I expect things to pick up over the weekend since we have a lot of good reservations already!

I know right!? That's the main reason I took the job. I love telling people what books are engaging or informative or even boring. I have a little section for my books of the week. Well, I would expect to be busy over the weekend for sure if people are already booking reservations. Hopefully you're not slammed out of control.

Being totally slammed isn't the worst thing in the world! I like to keep busy and to make good tips, but it can be exhausting for sure. How long have you been working at your current job? Is it something you see yourself doing long term?

Well I recently just stumbled upon it. After college and my parents kicking me out I needed to find work. What a better job than turning your hobby and love of reading into a paycheck. I get the idea of being slammed being a good thing. I love it when the store has something going on and we are just slammed with people. I hope I can open my own bookstore one day. I found my passion. What about you and the restaurant? Do you want to be there long-term?

dialog.text: What sort of volunteering does your mother do?

That's great. It feels good when we help people. I have volunteered homeless children with food and studies. How is your part time going on at diner?

That is amazing. i occasionally go with my mother to help out, it such a satisfying experience to help those who need it. My job is going well thankyou, just sometimes people can be so rude, i don't get it.

Oh wow that amazing. Do you create your own music? Yes i love travis Scott his music is great.

You sure are talented. Yeah music is a wonderful thing, i would like to go to one of his concerts.  Omg Italy that is my dream to go there. How long was you there for?

Italy is defiantly on my list of places i would like to travel too. And my sister is starting to get better at playing thank you for asking.

personas: I am a piano teacher.  I volunteer at a homeless shelter.
I have been to Italy.
I have not attended any basketball games.  I liked the food and music in Italy.
I would like to volunteer at a homeless shelter.  I play basketball.

I mostly play the second guard position in basketball.  If we win our district competition, we could play an Italian team.
My basketball tournament will be in Texas this year and in Europe next year.
I'm excited to go to Italy.  I want my parents to let me go to Italy.  My neighbor, Mr. Puccini, has relatives in Italy that will help me get cheap lodging.

dialog.text: I have booked 3 new clients for piano teaching. I am volunteering at a homeless shelter too now. Maybe you can join one time.
That is great!  As for volunteering, I would love to sometime.  Maybe after basketball practice tomorrow?
That would be awesome if you could come! what time is practice over?
Since school is off, our summer league has earlier practice.  It's supposed to be over at 2:30 PM.
Perfect! Definitely if you can come you should! How is basketball going? Team looking good this year?
I don't want to brag or jinx us too much, but we are looking pretty good. We have a couple all-staters on the team!  I think we are going to be the team to beat!
Love to hear that! Keep grinding you are a beast! What position are you playing this summer?

I am going to spend most of my time as the 2 guard, but I move to 3 in some sets.  They said if we win the league, we can play in a district wide competition and if we win that, we could represent our team against international competition.  It's not quite Italy, but I could play an Italian team!
Is the tournament going to be held into the states? You need to get to Italy as soon as possible! It is amazing!

I guess they alternate and this year it's going to be in Texas, but next year is supposed to be in Europe. If I'm still playing, who knows?  I heard they have pro basketball leagues there.  Did you attend any games?
I did not attend any games,  I mostly took in the food and music which was fantastic!
Oh, I can't wait to go.  I keep nagging my parents about it.  I think they are really considering it.  Our neighbor Mr. Puccini actually has relatives there and said we could get cheap lodging.

dialog.text: I watched a lecture by Marianne Williamson today that really inspired me to explore my spirituality even more.
Oh interesting. What kinds of things do you think you'll do? More yoga or reading? Or something entirely different?
I'll probably look for more lectures to watch and maybe that will lead to some interesting books to read.
Ah okay. There are probably some good podcasts out there, too. Have you thought of taking a trip somewhere? Peru was absolutely amazing.
Oh, tell me more about your experience with the shaman there, that sounds like it was a very eye-opening experience. do you try ayahuasca?
I did not, but I considered it. You know it's funny how I found the shaman. You'd think that stuff is so old school that it'd be hard, but they're totally online now and you can book them that way.
That's very convenient. I wonder if you can do the entire experience online, like a virtual meeting or something.
Maybe, but there's definitely something powerful about being there in person. I can't really explain it; it's an energy thing.
Is there a language barrier when you meet a shaman in Peru or does language not matter when it comes to these types of things?
Well, I speak some Spanish so that helps quite a bit.
What else did you do in Peru, did you exercise at all or climb any mountains?
Yeah, I did a lot of hiking. There are some beautiful places to see down there. You should go.

Yes. I look forward to Summer. I do high intensity interval training for my daily workouts and a bit of yoga
I like HIIT training.  I feel like I accomplish a lot in a relatively short amount of time. I hope you'll soon be able to move your yoga outside onto a deck. Seems like that would be zen.

That would be very interesting!  I would bet it is fairly easy to find online comparative religion courses from various universities or even community colleges.
Yes, I'm sure there a many sources. The research itself should keep me busy. Do you recommend any religions?

I have friends of all different religions and there are parts of each that resonate with me and other parts that leave me thinking "um, what?" ha ha  For me I find a general peaceful and accepting nature to be the way to live. Yes .I was raised Catholic but I'd love to continue my spiritual journey but learning about many more religions.

dialog.text: The weather up here is finally warming up, I did my yoga on the porch this morning.
That's awesome! Nothing beats doing yoga outdoors! What is your favorite time of day to do yoga?
My favorite time is the morning it helps me focus and stretches my body to get me ready for the day. What is HIIT training?

My favorite time of day to exercise is in the morning also. I call it 30 before 7:30 because I try to get in at least 30 minutes of HIIT before then. HIIT is High Intensity Interval Training. It is short bursts of working out as hard as you can, followed by short periods of resting. Alternating the two back and forth. It'll wake you up first thing in the morning for sure! Have you ever tried anything like that?
Yes I have. It is a pretty effective work. I was wondering what was your day job?
I'm an EMT during the day. It's tough work but definitely rewarding. And requires the fitness. What about yourself?

I am not working at the moment. I am focusing on my spirituality full time. Being here in Alaska closer to nature awakens feelings and desires to be closer to nature and the beyond. Have you ever had a spiritual awakening?

Wow that is amazing! I did actually, almost a year ago I was introduced to Abraham Hicks, and I've worked with a few spiritual coaches since then. I'm always studying the law of attraction. Do you have any books or spiritual guides you'd recommend me looking into?
The power of now, The spiritual guide which disentangles the soul and the book of joy are pretty good reads
That's great! Have you read The Secret?
No I have heard of it. Is it a good read?
It is! It's what many of the spiritual leaders base their teachings upon. It's kind of the holy grail of spirituality.

dialog.text: Tell me more about your spiritual awakening.
Well, it had a lot to do with the location and the accoutrements of the event. A very strange experience indeed.
Where did this experience happen? Does the environment make much difference?

At the time I was in the hills outside a small village in Peru. I payed for a 'Shaman' to take me into the hills so that I could have the experience that I was looking for. I would say the location matters a lot. You always want to be in a safe location during your spiritual awakening.
I agree. I am very spitirual but I think my journey has been more gradual than an awakening experience. I feel more grounded and centered with every day that practice.
I agree with that sentiment. All things in moderation right. Do you find that yoga helps you to feel more spiritual ,or in a sense, 'closer to god'?
I don't believe in a god per say, but I do feel much closer to the earth and myself during yoga.
Oh I bet, especially in Alaska I'm sure that feeling must be amazing!
During the light hours of the year it's wonderful, but we have months of darkness where I live and it can difficult to maintain that sense of spirituality.
I'm sure! It must get pretty sleepy over there. Months of hibernation huh.

haha yea. That's one of the reasons I had to quit my job because it was very difficult to keep my sleep schedule on track when there is no daylight. I'm sure you could handle it though, you seem tough.
I could try but I'm afraid I would also just spend days asleep haha.

I feel like I need some more hands on experience, like actually going into a hospital and working with their management staff, etc.  But maybe that's just me.

Oh of course. It's not for everyone. Your expertise is far more hands on so I completely understand why you would prefer to go to school in person. I agree, what's nice is that I've got a stable job and plenty of time to decide when and how to make the change. I'm sure that's something you've got going for yourself too.  Have you been up to anything else besides looking at schools lately?

That sounds really nice.  I need to start making some time for outdoor exercise again.  It's so good for both the body and the mind, don't you agree?

I agree completely. It makes you feel charged and ready to face the day. While it seems like it would tire you out it actually does the opposite in the long run. We both can start our routines up again!

I'm thinking working in a hospital might be better. It's depressing to watch all these lonely old people slowly declining with no one to visit them. It's taking a toll on me emotionally.

You're right, it takes a lot of heart to be in this profession. How do you like your job right now? I'm sure that it can get just as stressful.

This has to be the year! There's no other option. I'm hoping to be able to win back custody of my kids. It's unfair that their mother just took them away from me without the option of even being able to visit them.

dialog.text: I talked to my counselor and she is going to help me with all the paperwork to be a foreign exchange student, do you think you could write me a letter of recommendation?
Sure thing. Are you free at the weekend? We could meet up to sort it then.
Yeah, the weekend sounds great thank you so much! Is there a certain day that works for you? Are your softball games only on Tuesdays or do you ever have a game on the weekend?
Yeah softball is just on Tuesday. Sometimes we have games on a Saturday but I'm free this weekend. Have you decided where you want to go for the study abroad program?
I think Paris to be honest, it sounded so lovely when you were telling me about your visit with your Mom. I'm still working on my fluency in French.
Studying in Paris would really help you learn the language. Have you travelled to any other countries?
You are 100% right about that, I went on a vacation to Mexico a while back and that really helped me with my Spanish. I'm sure you've done a lot of travel with a military father.
Yeah I've travelled around Europe a lot. I love the UK and Germany too.
More travel in Europe is absolutely on my bucket list. Would you say Paris was your favorite? The Eiffel Tower is so beautiful, I can only imagine what it must be like to see it in person!
Paris is beautiful. Nice in France is beautiful too. The promenade and the pebble beaches are wonderful
Well, if I end up going to Paris to study you can come for a visit and we'll go all over, maybe by that time I'll be fluent enough to teach you some basics!
Yeah that would be great. Would you try any of the French food?

dialog.text: I just started my first French lesson.
Wow! How is the lesson so far?
Good! I forgot how difficult it is at the very beginning though. I'm so used to being fluent or at leasy pretty good!
Yeah, learning a different language is definitely a challenge. Does knowing Spanish help at all with understanding French?
It actually doesn't. The rules for masculine and feminine are kind of different so I'm having to unlearn some stuff I assumed too soon!
Oh wow! That sounds really complex! It seems like it would be a real challenge to have to unlearn things you were used to.
It really is. I know I'll get there though. How is softball going?
You definitely will get there! Softball is going great! It's really a nice way to relax.
That's so good to hear! I wish I was sporty. I was always a book nerd, lol.
Haha, well I wouldn't call myself sporty. It's just something I do in my free time to release stress from the day.
Still, if my release was running around rather than sticking my nose in a book I'm sure my respiratory system would be grateful
Haha, it's never too late to start! Maybe you can find something that combines your love of learning with something more active.

That's nice to hear! I actually don't know any other languages other than english. My work doesn't give time to learn new things.
That's totally fair. It is a real commitment to learn a new language, especially when you have a full time job. If you had the time, what language do you think you would want to learn the most?
I actually want to learn French. I always love the way they speak. I m sure i don't understand anything, but it sounds cool.
It is a beautiful language, and I am really enjoying learning it. I would love to visit Paris one day. Have you ever been?
Yes, i actually went to Paris once. But it was so long ago. My mom took me there when i was in high-school.
It's nice that she took you there! What did you do while you were there? Was it just the two of you?
Yes, my dad had his duties, so it was just us. We went to the popular places and the most amazing thing is the Eiffel Tower. We actually spend the whole day there.
Oh, so it was while your father was stationed nearby? Was he actually stationed in Paris or did you just take a trip from where he was?
Oh no, he didn't come. It was just me and my mom. He had this duties while we were planning our trip so he couldn't make it.

dialog.text: Did you have any softball games since we last talked?

Ok.  I know it's been so busy and I've been cramming as much French as my mind will take.  I think I've sprouted a beret out of my head!
Ha, I bet! It's still on my list to learn but I have no idea how I'll find the time. Have you given any more thought to going to Paris? You really should go!
I think about it all the time.  Do you remember much about it?  I hear it's pretty inexpensive in the fall, but I think I would have to take off some time for school to do it.
It's been a while since my mom and I went, but I do remember that it was beautiful. The Louvre is amazing. And the Eiffel Tower is just so worth a look.
Maybe I can ask my counselor about it.  I know there are study abroad options and I think I will know enough French to get by initially.
Oh, you'd be totally fine! Even back when I went, just about everyone in Paris spoke English so you'd be all good even without being fluent in French.
That's a good point!  You have me really thinking about it.  You know what, I think I will call my counselor and then attend your softball game to tell you all about it!
Sounds like a great idea to me! Especially the part about you coming to my game, haha.

No, lol. (Although I do talk to my plants.) I think Old Yeller would traumatize Dr. McBark since that story doesn't end so well for the dog.
Yeah, I've heard people talk to their plants. Funny. Ok, sorry about that horrible suggestion. How about just reading him the dog encyclopedia?

personas: I have a dog named Roscoe.
I am in school, I teach and work as a waitress.
I work with food bank volunteering.
Our school has a therapy dog.
Our therapy dog is Dr. Woofington McBark, he is 5 and a black lab.

dialog.text: Do you want me to sign you up for food bank volunteering? Of course, if you have some free time
Maybe this summer when school is out! Right now I am swamped with teaching and waitressing on the weekends. How is life going for you?
Life is going well so far.  Staying extremely busy at the food bank. It seems more and more people are in need.
It is true! I have been seeing more children with food insecurities come through my classroom then ever before!
It really is a shame.  How does the school system handle the insecurities?

There are a lot of kids who qualify for free meals so when school is in session they are getting at least two meals that day (breakfast and lunch). The summers are much harder. On the bright side the school has a new volunteer... a therapy dog kids can read to!
That's awesome.  What's the dog's name?
Dr. Woofington McBark! He is 5 years old and is a black lab.
Dr. Woofington McBark...that's so funny.  I bet the kids love having him around.  Does he sit and listen to them reading?

He usually lays down and sometimes he listens with his eyes closed, but he still is following the story! Yes the kids love having him around but so do all the teachers! He is such a self esteem boost to the kids struggling with sight words and sounding things out.
I can imagine.  Dogs are a great comfort and can sense when something isn't right.  I know my Roscoe brightens my day each time I see him.  So loving and caring.
What kind of dog is he?

personas: I have a dog and a cat.
My male dog is named Roscoe and my female cat is named Mean Girl. I am a volunteer and over the weekend I cooked lemon chicken to bring to people in need.
I love volunteering.
I can't leave my dog alone in my house.
I work at a center that needs volunteers.

dialog.text: My dog and cat had a little fight yesterday
Oh no, did either of them get hurt?
Nah, it was more just like hissing and barking.
Wow... I can just imagine the noises.  It was probably really loud.  Are they getting along okay now?

Yeah they seem to be getting along now that everything's settled. Mean Girl tried to grab some food from Roscoe's bowl and he wasn't having it. Like he saw her messing around in his bowl and went after her.
I can believe.that.  Dogs can be very territorial.  How has volunteering been going?
It's been going good, over the weekend I made a big amount of my mom's famous lemon chicken and brought it over to donate for that night's meal. It was a hit, thankfully.
Oh, that sounds delicious.  We could use your cooking skills at our center.
I could come over to help out for sure. I love volunteering. If I could do it as a career i would.
That would be amazing.  We can use all the help we get.  Are you available this weekend?
Yeah I am. I just can't leave my dog in my place, could I bring him with me?
Sure.  He would be a big hit with the people coming in.  Give them some happiness with their meals.

dialog.text: I left Roscoe at home and he tore up his dog bed!
Oh no! I wonder if Mean Girl had something to do with it and set Roscoe up to take the fall haha
Ha! That is definitely one way to look at it. But it was probably Roscoe. He had that guilty look on his face, you know?
I sort of remember. I wish I was home more and could get a pet. Such good companions. Dr. McBark will have to do for now, but he has made me decide I want a lab if and when I do get a pet.
I imagine he must be such a well-behaved dog! Labs are so sweet. I'm sure you'll have a pet someday. You see Dr. McBark at school lately?

Yes, I see him around pretty often, but I try not to interfere with him too much so he can save his energy for the kids who need him. I'm going to schedule him to come to my class so the kids can read to him soon.
That's great! I'm sure they'll be really excited. Would be nice if we could get a therapy dog at the food bank. I'm sure a lot of people could use that comfort.

That's true! Maybe you have an idea in there somewhere. Sadly, so many ideas that help the community require more funding than folks are willing to put in. It's so sad. It's so easy to see income disparities when I look at the kids in my classroom. It doesn't seem fair.
It's not fair at all. I'm grateful that I'm able to at least make some difference, I just wish there wasn't a difference that needed to be made!

Yes, and in my state teachers are so underpaid. That's why I have to wait tables too. I thought the purpose of society was to ultimately find a way where people can enjoy their lives instead of work work work. But no, instead all of the money lies in the hands of like 5 individuals. It's so gross.
It definitely is. And being a teacher is such an important and difficult job too. There's no reason a teacher (or anybody) should NEED a second job!

Exactly! A reliable salary is nice, but when I take what I make and break it down by the hour, it's indentured servitude basically. Not to mention the supplies and things I buy out of my own pocket because there's no room in the school budget for them. It's all such a mess. I'm sure you see so much of this and much worse at the food bank. If I ever got rich, I'd give so much back to my community. Truly! I wish everyone felt that way. Maybe seeing all the kids in my class makes me more empathetic to the struggles.

dialog.text: We had three deliveries in one night on my last shift. It made me think of your triplets.

This might be bad to say and don't tell my husband this, but I cannot stop thinking how expensive this is going to be. Having one child is already expensive, but three at once. I am freaking out!
That's valid. I'm sure he'll be putting in extra shifts at work to make up for all the expenses you'll have. Disneyland might have to wait for a while unfortunately.
I didn't even think about that!  When is the next time I can go to Disneyland? I might never get to go there again!
Ah, don't worry. I'd be happy to treat your whole family to Disneyland at some point to help you all relieve some stress. I've earned quite a few rewards during my visits.
I appreciate that so much, but I can't ask you to do that. Just the fact that you would even offer means so much to me. Thank you
Please, it would make me so happy to see you guys happy. Think about it. I'd be happy to babysit every once in a while too.

Why are you so increible to us? I'm not going to lie, I'm pretty sure I'd take you up on that babysitting sometime. Especially if the husband and I want to have a date night. But I promise I won't overdue it. We have already been looking at babysitters in the area
Oh, stop. I'm just being a good friend. You deserve some time to yourselves! It'll be really crazy with the babies for a while so you'll have to make the most of any time you can get.
Not just a good friend, but a great friend. I want you to know how much I appreciate you. thank you

I bet! Its so delicious, and will be very popular for cookouts I bet. It was especially good with the fresh cilantro from my herb garden. How's your grandaughter doing?
Fresh herbs always make a difference. I tell people that all the time. She's doing good! She's learning to make some of my recipes as well.
Oh, I'm sure she enjoys that. Of course the best part of making your recipes is eating them, haha. I made chicken tacos for lunch today just so I could eat some of the salsa. I ate so much.
Haha, it is I must agree! Chicken tacos are fabulous. I make one salsa that has white queso in it that is really good with tortilla chips.

I'll send that one in the email as well! I love cooking it's a big passion of mine.

dialog.text: How long have you been working in construction?
About four years, and I love being able to build structures for those who need it. How long have you been a tour guide?
I've been doing it for about ten years.  Before that I was a volunteer at the museum.  I do like doing the tour guide thing and helping people understand history.
That is very cool! What areas of history do you cover?
It is local history.  But that includes the Native American tribe that once lived and owned this land.
That's interesting, especially since you've been doing it so long. How long have you been gardening?

I grew up with gardens.  My mom grew rose bushes and we always had a vegetable garden.  There is nothing like picking the vegetables and then cooking them for dinner.  I know you said you don't garden, but I always recommend growing a few vegetables, it is so much healthier.
I might get into it. A lot of the meals I like to make at home incorporate fresh vegetables and fruits, especially my favorite Hispanic dishes. Maybe I could look into growing cinnamon.
I definitely have cilantro in my herb garden for when I make salsa.  Did you know that cinnamon comes from a tree?
I had no idea! I've always seen the sticks but I thought maybe there was a cinnamon bush or something. You'll have to send me your salsa recipe as well I'm sure it's delicious.
Oh, I am always tinkering with the salsa recipe.  I have never quite perfected it yet.  What is your favorite Mexican dish?

I love carne asada. My father had a friend growing up that would make it for Fourth of July and it was always really delicious. If you won't hand over the salsa recipe, do you have any good tea recipes? I know you mentioned loving chamomile tea.

dialog.text: I think I finally found the secret to the BEST salsa recipe!
Oh I love salsa with mexican food! What's the recipe?

I have basically perfected how to grow the best cilantro. It involves a lot of plant nutrients and tending to my garden, but it is worth it when combined with fresh jalapenos and tomatoes from my garden! What is the best salsa you have ever tasted?
I'm not sure to be honest. I've tried so many different kinds. I would be biased but I think my salsa is the best. I love making things like salsa and jams and jellies!
We might have to have a salsa competition one of these days then! Are you saying that you like to make fruit flavored salsa? That can be a lot of fun to experiment with.

That sounds fun! I love to make salsa with tomatoes and such. I also like to make jams and jellies.. but of course only when the fruit and veggies are in season and I can find them at the farmer's market.
Do you ever sell your salsa, jams, or jellies at the farmer's market? That is something I have always wanted to try. I figured it could be a nice side hustle!
I have sold them actually! But I always run out quickly. I just don't have enough ingredients to make a bunch of product. I don't garden.
Have you ever thought about trying your hand at it? I honestly find it really relaxing, and it is great not having to rely on anyone else for fresh veggies!
I have thought about it, but between my job and my volunteer work I just don't think I have the time it requires to keep it up.
That totally makes sense. If you ever get the free time, I highly recommend it! It can be a nice break from the stress of your job too.
Yes I've heard that! Currently my stress reliever is a good book and a hot cup of tea. They are always my go to!

dialog.text: Have you found anything else for your baby? How are the decorations going?

Not yet. I was looking at some strollers but I haven't decided on one yet. There are so many great options! It's hard to choose one. I think we are still leaning towards gender neutral colors like green and yellow.
Yeah I think that would be a good idea. If you are expecting a either a boy or a girl I think that's fine. Also, if you might have another child in the future, you can re-use some of the things.
Exactly! Hand-me-downs will definitely help cut back on expenses. What was your favorite part about pregnancy?
I just really felt like my baby was a part of me. It's hard to explain, but I felt so comforted that my future child was safe inside of me. I think that probably sounds sort of strange!
No it doesn't at all! I feel such a strong connection to this little peach inside of me. I can't wait until they are born! I am tired of the morning sickness though. I know it will all be worth it.
Yep, the morning sickness was the worst, but it is temporary. The years you will enjoy razing and being with your child will be worth it many times over!
I am going to have to try your suggestion of gingerale and crackers. I have been drinking coca cola but it hasn't been helping very much.

Thanks for the suggestion! How are your kids doing? Can you believe they are already 8 and 10?
They are doing great, and no! I can't believe how quickly they are growing up. TIme has flown by so much, try to enjoy it while you can.
I will! Would your kids be interested in babysitting when they get older? I have a feeling I am going to need some extra help!

dialog.text: I got a rock stuck in my cast and had to have it cut open early.  The doctor was really mad at me.

Maybe stay away from the skateboard for a while? That's great the doctor thinks the bone is healed. How will they know for sure? Does it feel better?
It was a hair line fracture. The cast was to try and keep me from injuring it more. They did an x-ray and it looked fine. It does feel better, thanks.
Well, that's great to hear. Does this doctor also handle your potential thyroid issue?
No, I handle that with supplements. After experiencing the broken arm, I know why you want to stay off the skateboard.

Yeah, given my age, I'm afraid to even think about how long it would take to heal. What did you miss doing most while you had your cast on? Besides skateboarding of course!
Being able to hold a cheeseburger properly. Its harder than you would think to get a burger in your mouth with a cast on.

Yes!  I don't know what I'd do if I saw one of them walking next to me!  You've got some beautiful animals in Australia, right?
Yes! Koalas and kangaroos are my favorites. They can both be a little vicious but as long as you're careful and respectful you can get close enough to watch them for hours. You should visit!
I'd LOVE to go there.  "On my bucket list" as they say.  I'll be there some day

dialog.text: I have a wrestling match this weekend.
Awesome!  Please let me know how it goes.  Have you been successful lately?
Not really, I feel like the booker is too concerned about elevating his friends rather than the people who are most talented.  It hurts both the promotion I am involved in, and myself, in my opinion.
I'm sorry.  Have you talked to him about your concerns?  Perhaps he can be persuaded to change.

Yes.  Given that the outcomes are pre-determined in Pro Wrestling, there is a great deal of politicking and sucking up that is expected.  The people who determine the outcomes always seem to want favors, while I just want to go where my talent takes me.  My conversation with him revealed that I would need to compromise and start sucking up, which I do not want to do.

Good for you for sticking to your guns!  But I have to say, maybe it's time for a change?  I grew up poor, you know.  I lived from job to job as I built up savings so that I could be stable.  But I was happy.  I did what I liked, and I felt I made a difference in the world.

That is one of the major issues.  Professional wrestling is basically a monopoly now, with one company far above all others.  There are not any other viable companies to go to, so the choice I have is basically giving up what I love, or compromising my values.  I do not particularly like either option. I suppose I could try to transition to UFC, I do have a significant amateur wrestling background which got me into professional wrestling in the first place.

I dunno.  I hear UFC is pretty brutal.  I admit I don't like the idea of anyone getting beat up for a paycheck.  But if that job is something you find joy in, something that makes you feel fulfilled, then I think it's worthy of consideration.  But I teach gym now.  It's a job that makes me feel happy because it makes others happy.  It's not the main job I would have signed up for at first...but I wouldn't change it for the world.

I would not pursue UFC out of a desire to hurt people, just to compete with other fighters.  What do you typically do during your gym classes?  I am always looking for ideas to add some variety to my cardio workouts, have you done anything interesting or outlandish during your gym classes?

You can probably tell I'm tired when I say I currently teach.  I did tell you earlier that I was retired.  And I still am.  But to answer your questions, I taught children.  I tried to keep things interesting by teaching trust-building exercises.  I would have the students try out each others' specialties in order to relate to one another.  Nothing too outlandish, but for one April Fools' Day...well, that's a story for another time ;-)

I know how that feels.  You get so caught up in a pleasant memory that you think it is still occurring.  I asked about your gym class experiences because mine were always so boring and "vanilla".  The strangest thing we did by today's standards was dodgeball, which would probably get a teacher fired nowadays.

Yeah, I never ran into issues with that.  We did dodgeball more than a few times.  The children liked it a lot.  One time we did it in the dark!  And THAT time...I did almost get fired when one of the children tripped and sprained their knee.

dialog.text: What was your profession before you retired?

That is good to hear, it is always fun to read about your passions! I wrote romance novels. Cheesy love stories where the woman was normally the hero, but I love them. Added a different story line to the normal love stories.
That is so cool! A feminist twist on romance is genius! I can't believe you were able to retire at just 32. What do you do with all your free time now besides browsing the internet?
Thank you! It was a risk, but following my gut paid off! I like to cook and research new vegan recipes. Do you have a favorite vegan recipe I can try out next?
I made vegan "chicken" fingers using oyster mushrooms a couple weeks ago! As a fellow vegan, I was really missing the crispiness of fried chicken. Is there anything non-vegan that you really miss?
Wow, that sounds amazing. I will be trying that this week! I hate to admit it but I miss the comfort of a good old cheeseburger from time to time.
That is SO fair. And I feel like it's so hard to find a really good vegan patty. Beyond burgers are okay, but the realness of the "meat" turns me off a little bit. I definitely miss cheese. A lot.
Oh my goodness, yes I miss cheese too! What made you decide to be a vegan?

A couple things. The environmental impact of meat and dairy products was what started my research into veganism. Then I started to read up on how poorly the animals are treated on dairy/egg farms and decided that I didn't want to be contributing to their pain.
Sounds like perfect reasoning! All similar reasons for me. Does anyone ever give you a hard time about that choice?

I find that it's all about using the right type of mushroom -- mild ones hardly taste like what they are, and make great substitutions. What substitutions do you use for vegan stuff?
The usual stuff.  I have aquafaba to replace egg whites.  I use vegan butter.  Obviously I find that the side ingredients are harder to properly substitute.  What do you think?
I've never used aquafaba. What is it? And yeah, it can be hard to replace certain things but other things are surprisingly versatile!

It's basically water from a can of chick peas.  It has the same density and texture as egg whites.  I just recently started using it.  I have just started expanding my vegan lifestyle so I am still in the beginning stage if you know what I mean?

OH MY GOODNESS I never knew that!!!! I should try it some time. I already use chickpea water to make nacho chickpeas (I don't drain them then mix in nutritional yeast and seasoninings). That's so smart of you. For a beginner you already have some great tips! Have you tried using nutritional yeast yet?
I have not!!!  What can you do with that?  You are turning in to a great resource for my kitchen habits!
nturitional yeast TASTES like cheese, but is actually a b12 powder
Oh my goodness.  That would be awesome to try.  I would imagine all that b12 would give you so much energy.

personas: I am looking for some vegan meal recommendations.

dialog.text: Do you have any vegan meal recommendations for me?
I do!  A vegetable pizza with broccoli, peppers and onions.  Use fresh ground flour for that fresh taste.  When you get the texture of the vegetables just right, it tastes amazing.
How do you recommend I prepare the vegetables?

Steam the broccoli first.  Make it a little under the texture you want because it will continue cooking in the oven.  As for the peppers and onions, I recommend you fry them on the stove lightly, just to give them a good char before you set them on the pizza.
That sounds really simple! I'd better make some extra to snack on while the pizza is cooking. What temperature do I need to have my oven on?
I do it at 400 degrees.  Others may suggest 350, but I really want to dig into that pizza ASAP lol
Fahrenheit? My oven only uses Celsius. I thought yours did as well. What is it in Celsius?
My oven actually does use Fahrenheit.  Although I'm from Germany, I live in the USA now and the ovens use Fahrenheit here.  As for converting to Celsius, it's a simple math problem.  5/9 * (F - 32)
Oh! I didn't realize you were in USA now. Ok, so about 200C. That's simple enough! I like to put olives on my pizza as well sometimes. How do you feel about that?
Olives are great!  I try to avoid the salt, however, since my doctor told me to cut down on that.  But they really do pep up a pizza.
They really do! Also some peri-peri sauce and basil can really make it come alive. Can you get peri-peri where you are now?
Not really.  I've looked around.  It's sold on Amazon, though, so I don't have to make it myself ;-)

I do, along with olives. But they are so filled with sodium, I can't have them anymore.

i wonder if garlic and vinegar heavy pickles would be less sodium-y for you. you'd still get that acrid taste. it can be so hard to just cut salt right out! Is that the main dietary change you've been making?
I've cut out a lot of meat as well! I really like eating rice and beans as well as hummus and veggies.
I bet I could easily give up meat. It's not really my thing. I like cheese, sauce, etc and other ways to create flavor. And I'm super into hummus, too! What flavor hummus do you like?
I like the lemon kind, it's sour and flavorful at the same time. What's your favorite?
I love red bell pepper hummus. And I recently found a recipe for buffalo hummus -- it's delicious and it hits that hot wing craving! Do you like spicy stuff?
Not so much. Does the buffalo hummus have blue cheese in it? I'm trying to avoid dairy.
nope, no blue cheese. it has ranch seasoning and buffalo sauce and garlic and onion powders, then the traditional hummus stuff. i avoid dairy too -- hurts my tummy!

dialog.text: I started a new piece of art.  It is my interpretation of the "Big Bang" (the birth of the universe).  Do you want to see it?  Maybe you can give me some ideas to improve upon it.
Sure! I would love to give you my opinion on it. I recently started an abstract piece. I'm trying to combine something that looks like the ocean and the sky colliding.
I like that idea very much.  I love anything inspired by outer space.  I sold a few paintings like that in my past.
If you don't mind my asking, what is the highest amount you've sold a painting for? I've yet to have the courage to sell any of mine.

My most expensive sale was over $5k, but try not to use that as a guide because I was a professional painter in my old life.  I suggest painting for the love of it and take any profits as the cherry on top.
Absolutely! I think if you follow your passion in life the money will follow. Do you attend any art trade shows or go to any museums? Where do you find most of your inspiration?
I don't attend many exhibits anymore.  I draw my inspiration from my past.  I had a very difficult life and it is very therapeutic to paint about it.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. It's great that you've found a therapeutic way to handle that burden.
Thank you.  I was actually able to use the profits from my paintings to get away from my troubles and branch out on my own, so art has been a real life-saver for me.

dialog.text: I finally finished my latest piece and I'd love your feedback on it.

I take them to street fairs mostly. I do pretty well there, depending on the city.
That seems like a good idea. When you create a painting, do you think about what your customers might buy, or do you just paint what feels right for you?
I try and do both. Paintings that might be "popular" will draw the customers in to my booth. There they will see my other stuff and maybe they will be a repeat customer.

I am obsessed with abstract art - but I am not sure that is what sells well. I think it's hard to balance being artistic with being a business and making money. It looks like you were able to balance the two, is it something you want to keep doing?
Well it's what I'm good at, so I don't really have a choice. But I do enjoy it, though like I said I don't do the pretentious art exhibit thing anymore.

Yeah, I hate that pretentious stuff too, but that's where the money is. I can't work at Burger King forever. I was thinking of doing a painting of different burgers, do you think that's a good idea for an art topic?
Like a Warhol Campbell's soup thing? I like it! I'd buy one for sure.
Yes! I love how Andy Warhol lived by his own rules. That's really inspiring to me. He made a ton of money that way too. What inspired your paintings?

Well I liked to create futuristic paintings because my reality was so depressing. It was a way for me to escape to another world. You could probably channel something similar with the way your family treats you. Put that angst into your work.

Ah, ok. So the paintings were about a world you wanted to see. Angst is a good topic for art I think. Some of the best music comes from expressing anger.  It's just when you see a lot of art, it's all flowers and kittens. I think painting a burger elevates the common to something glorious. I want people to think of burgers in a new way, like you did with your futuristic paintings.

oh swimming, that is great! i wish i was a strong swimmer. my kids do more or less enjoy the same activities for now. i think that will probably change as they get into high school. we will see. how old were you when you got into farming?

i would love to come and stay with the kids! that sounds like a ton of fun. let's plan it. and i definitely know what you mean. you will find out once and for all what you are truly meant to do. it was smart of you to venture out and try something new

i think they don't really know yet. one of them is really good at math, and the other one isn't as much into school. but they are both so young. i think spendign some time on the farm would really show us how much of a work ethic they really have!

What is the best way to learn songs? Do you teach yourself? I looked up the spanish word for guitar and it is "la guitara"

I think you have inspired me! I am going to look into it. It helps bring out my creative side! That is so impressive you can mimic songs just by listening. I wish I had an ability like that. Ah yes. Good thing there are plenty of seasons of reruns to watch! The farm keeps me busy. It is hard for now, but I am sure i will miss it when I am gone, so I try to take the time to enjoy it. Do you make your kids do a lot of chores around the house?
Absolutely, most of the time they are a big help around the house but there are times when they can be very lazy and messy! Do you have any kids?
No kids for me, unless you count my many animals as my kids! They keep me busy enough. I guess they will help prepare me for kids one day though. How old are yours?

Those sound like fun ages! Law school can be a pain, I learn a lot but I am looking forward to being done and getting out there in a real world. Actually getting paid for all my hard work! That's the plan at least

That's awesome! I love looking at other bikes and getting to know people who share the same interests as I do. Barbecue is one of my favorite types of food. I love it too! They serve Mexican food art my restaurant. You should try it one day, I'll bring you all of my personal favorites!

Oh you wont regret it, they have some seriously amazing food at my restaurant. I absolutely love to cook! Cooking is one of my secret passions along with baking. I could teach you some simple recipes, it is really simple and fun once you get the hang of it. Especially the baking!

Baking sounds fun, too. I love cookies, brownies, cakes, and pies. Then again, who doesn't? Maybe you can bake something and take your bike up into the mountains for a picnic. Do you like going outdoors? Because I like hiking and birdwatching when I have the time.

Yum, those are all things I could eat every single day! Yes that would be delightful. Driving up the mountain and then enjoying a picnic of only dessert foods! I love the outdoors. Me and my parents used to go camping all the time when I was younger. Being an only child has its perks sometimes, we always went on vacations and did fun things outside on the weekends. What about you, did you and your family ever go camping?

That sounds like fun. I was just the opposite of you. I have a big family. With three older sisters and a younger brother, it always fun to go out there and go camping. I loved hiking. I loved listening to ghost stories. I loved cooking food over an open flame. Do you think you'll ever plan on camping like you did back then anytime soon?

You know, I think it probably would have been more fun if I had siblings to play with. Ghost stories are my favorite! I love all the myths and legends about ghosts and if they are real or not. Its all so interesting to me. Do you think ghosts are real? Yes of course, I plan on going camping next month actually, we are having a huge camp out with a bunch of my friends. You should come if your not busy!

I think ghosts aren't real but sometimes the wind will blow a certain way and I have my doubts! Ha! I think that might be why I enjoy camping so much. I love to hear about myths and legends, too. Being a dog trainer is busy work, so I'm not sure when I'll have the time to visit. But I think it would be a lot of fun to get to know each other better over some cookies next to a campfire. Maybe you can send me a recipe so I can practice before then. I'd love to start learning how to bake and I'm sure you're as good as you say you are.

If I'm traveling long distance I usually do but I was going slow around the island. I know the roads like the back of my hand and it came as such a shock. Was your friend ok?

Well, I think if the kids are too close in age, that's probably too much to handle, so maybe two years is the right about of time. Do you think your robot would have an opinion on that topic?
Im sure that my robot would hate that topic, it hates pretty much everything. Do you hope that all of your children will be girls?

I don't care about their gender, really, as long as they're healthy. It will be interesting to see their different personalities. Do you think that personality is something that comes from the environment, or is it pre-programmed in their DNA?
That is a good perspective to have. I think that some of it comes from DNA, but most of your personality comes from your environment.
Like your robot, for example, does it hate everything because it learned that from it's surroundings? Or was it programmed to be grumpy?
I think robots are a little different then people when it comes to that aspect. My robot can only do what it was programed to do, so it only knows how to be grumpy.

You are probably right, I think children come a little pre-programmed, but also change because of their environment. Do you feel that you are pre-programmed, or did you learn to like the things you like because of your experiences?
I believe that they can come out slight pre-programed but that their environment can change that throughout their life.
Yes, like I think I have a natural gift for gymnastics, but my parents signed me up for classes, too. Was there something that got you into robots and computer games?

My parent sent me to science camp in 6th grade and ever since then i have been in love with robots. How the get put together, how they are programed, it is all just so fascinating to me. When your parents signed you up for classes, did that help you become a better Olympian?
Absolutely! I was lucky to find the right coach. Talent alone isn't enough to make it as an Olympian. Which makes me wonder: do you ever think they'll have an olympic competition for robots?

dialog.text: So far things are going really well with my new friend. I would love to get some of your famous cookies to share with them!
That's great news! Should I decorate the sugar cookies in any particular way? Maybe with hearts and kisses?

Well, it is only going to be our third date, so it might be too soon for hearts and kisses. But my new friend loves cats and dogs as much as I do. Maybe you could put cats on half of the cookies, and dogs on the other half?
That would be adorable. I have been experimenting with some new design styles, so this will be a good opportunity. What will you do for your next date?

Well I was thinking we might go to a bakery for our next date, but since you are providing me some baked goodies, I think I'll take them to the zoo. I love to go to the monkey house and spend hours watching them playing and jumping all over the place!
The animal cookies will be right on theme. Maybe I can try my hand at some monkey cookies as well. Do you feel optimistic about this relationship?

So far so good. We are getting along really well. Lots of times we finish each others' sentences. It is really cute to see us together. Hey, do you think you could make pumpkin cookies instead of sugar cookies?  Or maybe even coconut cookies.  I'd love to try anything unique you feel comfortable trying to make for me.

I'm glad to hear it's going well. You know we older people like to relive our youth through people like you! I don't know if it's a good idea to try a new recipe unless you're sure your friend would like something like that. Some people don't care for coconut or pumpkin flavored things. I suggest you stick with the classics until you know they would enjoy something different.

Okay, since your most famous cookies are the sugar cookies, let's stick with that choice. Forgive me for being so forward, but I want to ask you if you feel too old to date anymore, or are you still carrying a dream of finding your true love still?  You are single, right?

I don't mind you asking at all. I had such a long, lovely marriage with my husband that I don't feel much need for more romance in my life. My grandkids have helped me get connected to some new friends who also enjoy baking and knitting, and they are pushing me to try new things as well.
That is really good to hear. I'm glad you had such a wonderful relationship. I hope someday I can say that I was as fortunate!

I hope that for you also. Of course, as a young, single person, you have so many opportunities to experience and enjoy the world. I married so young that I didn't have many of those chances when I was young. Although I'm having some of them now!

dialog.text: I just found the best place to travel to with the yacht.

that's hilarious. on a more serious note does your son play the guitar?

is that like NERF wars or something? you are lucky he is into mountain biking that's really good for his fitness. lots of kids these days don't get enough exercise and are overweight!

no you're right that's it. LARPING. To be honest it's probably better that he's into that than something else!
That's what I am thinking. Though even if he gets into being a furry or my little brony or whatever I will love and accept him no matter what.

Yes, when I get the chance. I like to spend time outdoors, so I look for good campgrounds and such. How is your band doing? Do you have any trips coming up?

Camping is fun. The band is doing pretty good. It's a little slow getting going, but we do ok. We have our trip to Missouri and we're working on getting something set up in Tennessee, hopefully it will work out.
That is awesome! What kind of venues do you play? Have you played in Nashville yet?
Not yet, but that would be awesome. Mostly we just play small bars and events. Some county fairs, things like that. It's a lot of fun. You should come see us sometime.
I would love to! Maybe when you are near me, I'll hit up a show! Does your son travel with you on your gigs?
Sometimes he does, it depends on where we're going. He likes when we play fairs. And then we turn it into a vacation and go camping or something, too.

No, he's not at all interested in music. Right now he wants to be a professional BMX racer!

I haven't purchased any cat toys off Etsy. I usually get them from the pet store, as I like to see and feel them before I buy them. How was the pizza?

It was good as expected. Pretty much any pizza with olives on it is good. I don't think I've had a bad one in my life. I was thinking about getting a cat nip toy off of Etsy. I love watching cats go nuts on cat nip.

I think olives are an acquired taste. Luckily, I've acquired it! I like olives on my pizza, too. My cats don't really like catnip. They get a little hyper for a short period of time, then they get bored and leave it. I've tried a couple of times, but with the same result. Now ping pong balls drive them crazy!
Hmm, I've never tried to ping pong balls thing. I'm going to have to get some and see what my cat does. Any other toys your cats like?

The ping pong balls are great. And they're cheap, so I don't mind when I step on them and break them! Tag and Henry bat them all over the house. They bounce off the furniture and base boards and really move on the hardwood floors of our house. They do get stuck under furniture, but I just use a broom to scoop them out. It is getting harder to bend down with my belly getting bigger. Laser pointers are another good toy for cats, and easy on my back!
That sounds like a lot of fun for the cats. I wonder if they are playing a game against each other that only they know about. The laser pointer sounds like fun as well.

Yeah, it seems like it sometimes. When one gets going, the other joins in. It's like they're talking to each other, "Hey, come on. Let's play!" The one drawback with the laser pointer is that there is only one, so they compete a little bit with each other. The looks they give each other are priceless!
Haha, that sounds like so much fun. I am going to be doing some searching on Etsy now to find these things. Do your cats ever try to eat your birds?

No, they pretty much ignore them. I think they know they're not food. But the birds get nervous around the cats, for sure. They quickly become silent when the cats are around. I keep the birds in a separate room, so as to not stress them out. The birds outside are fair game though. I often get little presents on the porch after the cats go out.
I've had my cat do that as well. They've also brought back some little rodents, like chipmunks.
My yard is mostly gopher-free because of Tag and Henry. It's a little bit gross, but I guess it's their nature to hunt, even if it's not for food.
